Subject: RE: MSA redline: audit language and pen-test scheduling

Folks —

I reviewed BlueHarbor's annotated redline and proposed the following compromise language and operational guardrails to present back:

- Audit rights: carve out two paths — (A) standard annual SOC 2 Type II delivery plus monthly consolidated evidence dumps (customer-facing artifacts and logs); OR (B) a single annual customer-requested inspection-lite (sampling-based) with clearly defined scope (service endpoints, tenant-scoped logs) and a maximum 48-hour remote staging access window.
- Pen-test: accept one annual customer-requested external pen-test with 30-day notice, subject to rules-of-engagement (ROE) that prohibit testing against live production databases and require a pre-test scoping call.
- KMS/HSM: for private/on-prem deployments, we can support customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM integration). For hosted customers, we offer Bring-Your-Own-Key (BYOK) options with limited HSM controls per standard architecture.
- Evidence cadence: propose a standard 14-day evidence sprint cadence during onboarding/critical review, and monthly consolidated drops post-onboarding. This gives BlueHarbor the ability to accelerate handoffs without forcing an ongoing operational burden on our ops team.

I've drafted redlines in proposed_security_exhibit_redwood.docx that try to keep the MSA footprint small while documenting the MAP approach and scheduling templates for pen-tests. If you all are comfortable, I recommend we send a single reconciled redline back to BlueHarbor and include a one-page MAP that lists dates and owner actions (SOC2 delivery, pen-test window selection, evidence sprint windows).

Karthik Iyer
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
